authorization: After Free Ask's release the owner asked to do the stored answers for suggested questions and the two small Free Ask follow-ups "systematically end to end full send", adding: "there should be some way to regenerate it as well so we don't get stuck with the same cached answer forever".
Asked before release, the owner chose "Release now".

release.reviewFindings: GPT-6.1 Sol (xhigh) approved #507 in 2 rounds (a waiting question the reader edited; a refresh after a failed standing read) and #509 in 3 (the stored bypass limited to a first question; a fresh answer waiting for the standing; the session checked before serving; a fresh answer and a follow-up never racing). The CodeRabbit CLI found one minor in #507 (declined: a refusal crossing midnight in flight) and three in #509 (fixed). CodeRabbit's PR review on #509 raised three: two fixed (the verse recorded as readers see it; translation in the key, no storing without Scripture) and one declined (stored suggestions in the over-cap 400; none can exist). CI quality-gates passed on both and on main.

steps.convex: Pushed main at ad90ce8e to prod unique-impala-244: the storedAnswers table with three indexes, an hourly cleanup, and the stored-answer reads and writes. No deletions.

changes: The first complete answer to a suggested question ("What does John 1:5 mean?", "Summarize John 1 so far", or the historical context at a first verse) is stored and served to later readers instantly, with no model call, no free answer and no credits.

A stored answer shows "Saved answer · Get a fresh answer": the fresh answer is asked like any question and replaces the stored one for everyone. Stored answers expire after 30 days, change with the model, rules, translation or chapter-so-far context (the key), and the owner can remove a verse's with storedAnswers:removeForReference.

A question asked before the free standing loads waits for it instead of opening the credits dialog; a failed standing read lets the server decide; a used-up refusal is read again just after midnight UTC.

smoke.after: Production, John 1:6, translation web. A new guest's quote listed no stored suggestion and 20 free answers; "What does John 1:6 mean?" was answered by openai/gpt-6-luna in 3.3 s, billed free, and then the quote listed it as stored (19 left). A second new guest's quote listed it as stored with 20 free answers; the question came back from storage (stored: true, billingStatus stored, 88 ms on the server, identical text) and the guest still had 20. That guest's fresh: true request was answered by the model (free) and replaced the stored text, which a third new guest then received from storage.
